reasoning_traces.think:
SA-MSCP addresses the core challenge of aggregating uncertain forecasts while maintaining valid probabilistic intervals. It begins with expanding-window cross-validation to gather residuals reflecting forecast uncertainty at multiple origins. These residuals are then centered and segmented into overlapping blocks to preserve temporal structure. Block bootstrap resamples these blocks to simulate future paths, which are stitched together to form stochastic trajectories. Each trajectory is aggregated into targets such as annual totals or growth rates. Finally, empirical quantiles across all simulated paths yield calibrated intervals. The method avoids naive combination of pointwise intervals, which fails due to induced dependence and nonlinearity in aggregation. Its strength lies in combining conformal prediction principles with simulation techniques tailored for complex forecasting tasks.
